title: Typing Async Code and Migrating JavaScript

questions.prompt: What type does an `async` function that returns a `number` have?

options.text: Promise<number> — async functions always return a promise

questions.explanation: An async function wraps its return in a promise, so returning a number gives the type Promise<number>.

questions.prompt: What type does `response.json()` resolve to, and how should you handle it?

options.text: The exact shape you expect; use it directly
any — treat the result as unknown and validate it with a type guard before using it

questions.explanation: json() resolves to any, which disables checking. Treat network data as unknown and validate its shape at runtime before trusting it.

questions.prompt: Under `strict`, what is the type of the value in a `catch` clause?

options.text: unknown — because JavaScript can throw any value; narrow it before use

questions.explanation: With useUnknownInCatchVariables (part of strict), the caught value is unknown, since anything can be thrown. Narrow with instanceof Error first.

questions.prompt: Which options help you include and type-check JavaScript during migration? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: allowJs includes .js files, checkJs / @ts-check type-checks them, and JSDoc adds types before renaming. noEmit is unrelated to migration.

questions.prompt: You can add a comment ______ at the top of a .js file to type-check it without renaming. (the exact comment, e.g. // @xxx)
questions.explanation: // @ts-check enables type checking for a single JavaScript file using inference and JSDoc — a low-friction migration step.

questions.prompt: Order these steps for gradually migrating a JavaScript codebase to TypeScript.

items.text: Add TypeScript and set allowJs so .js and .ts coexist
Turn on checkJs / // @ts-check and add JSDoc types
Rename files from .js to .ts one at a time
Tighten the config by enabling strict options incrementally

questions.explanation: Introduce TypeScript with allowJs, check JavaScript in place, rename file by file, then tighten strictness — all while the code keeps running.
